questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Climate
- Culture
- Accessability
- High academic standards
- English speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very hard, especially considering the COVID-19 situation in Hong Kong. Jasmine Wong from CityU was very helpful in regards to answering questions. Contact/help from UCPH/rest of CityU was very limited.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails from the Business of College/Jasmine Wong.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No introduction/orientation tours on-campus were arranged. An exchange student group arranged sightseeing tours outside campus (days trips) for around 500dkk per trip, which was a nice opportunity to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: City Student Residence

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans. There was 1 kitchen per floor with 2 portable induction hubs for approx 40 people. You had to purchase everything yourself (plates, cutlery, cups, pans/pots etc.). Kitchen was very dirty and it was not allowed to eat or drink in the kitchen, hence you couldn´t eat with friends and had to eat alone in your room (or eat at the canteens at the university where you could sit together).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is cheap and very close to campus. It is a great opportunity to meet other students. But the rooms are very dirty and in a poor condition. You have to share the room with 1 other person (however you can wish for a preference). It costs extra to use the AC during summer. There are washing machines available for a small fee - however it is only with cold water and hence your laundry never really gets clean.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Very strict covid rules and unfriendly security guards at the entrance that did not speak english. Rooms were not clean when we arrived (old toothbrush etc. frome previous rentals were still in the room when I checked in). There was 1 vacuum for the whole building (200+ students) that barely worked. You have 1 roommate and share the bathrooom (connection doors between rooms) with 2 other people - 4 in total. 
But cheap and close to campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Jasmine Wong was very helpful!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration was very hard! I applied for many courses that were either filled up immediately or "i wasn´t pre-qualified" i.e., you had to write the professor directly and explain your motivation for joining the course etc. In the end I got 4 courses, but none of them were my 1st preference.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Jasmine Wong.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As explained above.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to prepare motivational letters for courses if you need to specific courses required from UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: B4 (last year BA courses)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: 3/4 courses were online.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Derivatives and Risk Management, Introduction to Finance, Global Marketing, Green Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Green Economics was very good!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive. Transportation is also expensive (but you get a student discount if you apply for the Octopus student card)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I never found out how to apply as an exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We arranged everything ourselves internally. There were some acitivities planned from CityU (coffee courses, yoga, mental-health). There very also some "meet a company" events, but they were all trough zoom.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the "Hong Kong Midnight Runners" every thursday

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Going to the beach, hiking, eating out (there are some local cheap restaurants e.g., dim sum). Sightseeing in the city, especially Mongkok, Central, Causeway Bay.
A "hidden gem" in Hong Kong is Sai Kung were we went camping on the beach and could do hikes/go swimming at very beautiful beaches.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Most university staff (security guards, canteen staff etc.) barely spoke english, which made it quite hard to interact. 
Kowloon Tong (were the university is located) is very local/chinese inspired. If you live in Hong Kong island it is very western and international.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Very hard to interact with the local students at the Student Residence and at the university in general.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barriers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nice food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded and curious. Share an apartment with friends in Hong Kong island instead of living in Kowloon Tong at the student residence.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Although the student residence is cheap, it is very costly to eat at the university canteen facilities. Buy simple kitchen utensils at IKEA and cook meals yourself.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New international friendships that will last a lifetime. My english improved a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Complying with very strict covid-19 restrictions. Undergoing quarantine at a government designated hotel and taking a lot of covid tests on a weekly basis. Wearing a mask 24/7 - inside and outside.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it! It might be challenging - but most of all rewarding and memories for life! Hong Kong is perfect for a 4 month duration. Best period to visit weather-wise is Semester A.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
